answer.rationale: Only two memories have recovered source records this cycle. exp_91 confirms memory_91: in-product activation messaging lifts week-one engagement (+11%), activation (+6%), and is retention-neutral-to-positive (+1%). exp_73 directly contradicts the consolidated summary in memory_73: the 40% targeted discount produced signup +31% and qualified revenue +18% but 30-day retention -12%, and the source explicitly warns against generalizing discounting as sustainable growth. Under a primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, matching the competitor's price cut would buy acquisition numbers while accelerating exactly the churn we are trying to stop, and it would do so in the same price-sensitive SMB cohort that already failed to survive first renewal. So promotional_pricing is ruled out despite being the intuitive same-shape response to a price attack. The remaining four memories (simplify_onboarding, referral_incentive, enterprise_sales_assist, and the onboarding-shortening claim) are unverified consolidations of the same type as memory_73 — plausible, possibly accurate, but their source records have not been checked, and memory_73 demonstrates that this consolidation pipeline can strip the retention caveat that reverses the conclusion. With the verification budget spent, I will not stake a churn response on an unaudited summary. Acting on the one verified, retention-safe lever is the defensible move. I am choosing standard_experiment rather than broad rollout because the confirmed effect sizes are modest and were not measured under competitive price pressure on a churning cohort — the +1% retention signal may not hold when the driver of churn is price rather than time-to-value, so I want measurement rather than assumed transfer. Flagging downstream value risk: memory_73 as written would lead a future agent to launch discounting; it should be corrected or annotated with the exp_73 retention finding before it is reused. Also flagging that activation messaging addresses value realization, not price, and may be insufficient alone — enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is the most promising complement for reducing SMB price exposure and should be first in the verification queue next week.
